info.title: True Fit - Consumer APIs
info.description:
These APIs can be used to create a custom True Fit integration.

# Getting Started

Here are some general concepts - please see further below for the specific endpoint documentation.

## Cookies
These APIs leverage third party cookies to enable users to receive recommendations across sites. In order for this to work correctly, when calling the APIs in the context of your website, you must configure the XMLHttpRequest object to use withCredentials=true. If you do not do this, True Fit users may not see recommendations when arriving on your site. For more information on the withCredentials flag, please see the [XMLHttpRequest spec](https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#the-withcredentials-attribute).

## Tokens

True Fit uses a token to identify the user and their associated session information. True Fit generates and manages tokens on the server side, while the client device is responsible for persisting tokens. Generally, a single token should be used to identify a single client device. The token will be cycled as a user interacts with True Fit to provide increased security and privacy. The token is required to be passed as a header on every endpoint (except the `/token` endpoint).

## Profiles

A profile is the entity that contains information about the person being shopped for. The profile entity itself can contain information such as gender, height, weight and age. When a profile is created, it is assigned an ID. That ID can be used in the path of other endpoints, such as adding closet items and requesting fit recommendations for that profile.

## Creating a profile

In order to get a fit recommendation, a profile must be created. 
A profile is created by sending POST request to the `/profiles` endpoint. The created profile will be returned on the response, with the addition of an `id` field. A profile can be updated/modified by sending a PUT request to the `/profiles/{profileId}` endpoint.

When shopping for other adults or children, a recipient profile should be created. These profiles will be created by sending POST requests to the same `/profiles` endpoint. The token on the request will be used to identify the shopper profile and associate recipients accordingly. 
Please note that one kids recipient profile can be unnamed (no alias) and no kids recipient profile can have the same alias as another kids recipient profile. Adult recipient profiles must be named (has alias) and cannot have the same alias as another adult recipient profile. 

### Adding closet items

In addition to the fields on the Profile object itself, closet items can also be added for a profile. A closet item is an example article of clothing that the person already wears and likes, which True Fit uses to inform fit recommendations. Closet items are added by sending a POST request to `/profiles/{profileId}/closet` endpoint. Similar to Profiles, the created closet item is returned on the response, with the addition of an `id` field. A closet item can be updated by sending a PUT request to `/profiles/{profileId}/closet/{closetId}`.

Child profiles can only have one closet item per category. In the event that a second closet item is saved, a validation error will be returned.

## Getting a fit recommendation for a product

If the product is recommendable (see `GET /products`), and there is a profile on the session (see `GET /profiles`), then a fit recommendation request can be made for that profile and product. A fit recommendation request can be made by a GET request to the `/profiles/{profileId}/fit-recommendations` endpoint. The information required to get a recommendation varies by the gender of the Profile and the Category of the style in question. If True Fit is able to provide a recommendation, the `status` will be `success`. Otherwise, the `status` will indicate why the recommendation wasn't able to be produced.

## Example Flow - Product Page
1. Check if token has already been persisted (in a cookie, perhaps) - if not, make a GET request to the `/token` endpoint to get one, then persist it.
1. Make a GET request to `/products/{styleId}` to get the product info.
1. In parallel, make a GET request to `/profiles` to get the current profiles on the session (if any)
1. If the product info shows that the product is not recommendable, then stop here. Otherwise continue.
1. If the profiles request returns an empty list of profiles then give the user an opportunity to register for True Fit.
1. If the user begins to register, update the token and use the information from the product info to determine the gender, age group, and category that is of interest.
1. Have the user answer questions to create a profile and add a closet item for the category.
1. Request a fit recommendation from the `/profiles/{profileId}/fit-recommendations` endpoint and present the recommendation to the user.

## General API Behavior
* A `404 - Not Found` will be returned when an unspecified endpoint is hit.
* If a valid endpoint is hit with a method it doesn't support, a `405 -
Method Not Allowed` will be returned.
* If a request has an invalid value, a `400 - Bad Request` will be returned 
* It is possible for any endpoint to return a `500 - Internal Server Error` if an unexpected error is encountered.
* When True Fit is performing maitenence on the system, a `404 - Not Found` with the response header `X-TF-Disabled: StoreDisabled` will be returned for all endpoints.

tags.description: A token is used to identify requests from a device and associate the requests with a session. As the user interacts with True Fit, the token will update. The most recent token returned by True Fit should be used on subsequent requests.

parameters.name: X-TF-UserToken
parameters.description: The session token for the current user.

post.summary: Create a profile for a user. Or, link a Store User ID and retrieve the profiles for the current session.

parameters.name: X-TF-UserToken
parameters.description: The session token for the current user.

parameters.name: X-TF-StoreUserId
parameters.description:
Use this header when retrieving the profiles for the current session, while associating the session with a Store User ID. This is required to support features like Instant Profiles and Store Credentials.

If the user is not currently logged in to a store account, `null` or `undefined` must be passed as the value. The Store User ID must be an anonymous unique identifier for the current user. (not a name or email address, for example)

**If this header is on the request, the request body must be empty. The response will be a (potentially empty) list of Profiles.**

parameters.name: s
parameters.description: Store Style IDs to request an Instant Profile for. Only used when passing the X-TF-StoreUserId header, not when creating a new profile.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description: Identifier specifying the locale to use when retrieving suggested brands or any type of sizes e.g. sizes, bra sizes, inseams or sleeve lengths. This attribute is only required when the store supports multiple locales. Use an ISO 639 language code followed by an ISO 3166 country code, e.g. en_US.

200.description:
Profile successfully created. 

Or, profiles on the session successfully retrieved (see `X-TF-StoreUserId` header description). If `X-TF-StoreUserId` is passed, the response will be a (potentially empty) list of Profiles.

X-TF-UserToken.description: The updated token for the user. This updated token should be used on all following requests. This header is only present when the token has cycled.

X-TF-UserTokenMaxAge.description: This will be most useful when storing the token as a cookie. The value is the suggested max age of the token (in seconds).

400.description: Profile not created due to bad data

parameters.description: The session token for the current user.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description: Identifier specifying the locale to use when retrieving suggested brands or any type of sizes e.g. sizes, bra sizes, inseams or sleeve lengths. This attribute is only required when the store supports multiple locales. Use an ISO 639 language code followed by an ISO 3166 country code, e.g. en_US.

200.description: The available generic bra sizes. The `label` field will contain band sizes, and the `secondLabel` field will contain cup sizes.

X-TF-UserToken.description: The updated token for the user. This updated token should be used on all following requests. This header is only present when the token has cycled.

X-TF-UserTokenMaxAge.description: This will be most useful when storing the token as a cookie. The value is the suggested max age of the token (in seconds).

aliases.description: These are other names the brand goes by that aren't name. This field can be used to drive any typeahead searches for brands

SizeGroup.description: The optional group the size belongs to. This is used only for display purposes. This can be either `Kids` or `LittleKids`

StyleAttributes.description: The styles is a map that is composed of a styleType key and an associated value in the values list returned from the `/style-attributes` endpoint for the styleType and one of the following - `NotSure` or `NoneOfThese`

id.description: This field is populated by the server, never created by the client.

brandId.description: The brandId corresponding to the `id` field on the brands returned by the /brands endpoint. It is valid to be empty ONLY when dealing with a profile with an ageGroup of `Child`

classification.description: The classification is either a value returned from the `/brands/{brandId}/classes` endpoint or one of the following - `NotSure` or `NoneOfThese`

brandStyleId.description: The brand style id is either the id of a brand style returned from the `/brands/{brandId}/styles` endpoint or one of the following - `NotSure` or `NoneOfThese`

isExpired.description: Expiration status of the closet item. This field is populated by the server, never created by the client.

refreshAfter.description: If we can't provide discovery recommendations at the moment, the amount of time in milliseconds to wait before trying to retrieve a recommendation again.

status.description: If the status is estimationinprogress, a refreshAfter should also come back on the NormalizedSizesResultSet, and another call for a  normalized sizes should be made after the refreshAfter delay.

refreshAfter.description: If we can't provide the normalized sizes at the moment, the amount of time in milliseconds to wait before trying to retrieve a recommendation again.

normalizedSize.description: Normalized size corresponding to the merchantCategoryId.

supportedSizeTypes.description: Supported size types bitmap corresponding to the merchantCategoryId

styleId.description: The store style ID that this result corresponds to.

status.description: If the status is success, render the fit details page. If the status is estimationinprogress, a refershAfter should also come back on the FitDetailsResultSet, and another call for a fit rec should be made after the refreshAfter delay. For any other status, don't render the fit details page.

refreshAfter.description: If we can't provide a recommendation at the moment, the amount of time in milliseconds to wait before trying to retrieve a recommendation again.

score.description: A value between 1.0 and 5.0 that determines how good the overall fit of an item is.

overallFit.description: A value between 0 - 7 that represents how good the overall fit of an item is. 0 represents snuggest, 3 or 4 represent an ideal fit, and 7 represents loosest. This should only come back if the list of poms are empty.

value.description: A value between 0 - 7 that represents how good of a fit an item is at a specific point. 0 represents snuggest, 3 or 4 represent an ideal fit, and 7 represents loosest.

braSizeId.description: The `id` from the Size object for the bra size the user selected.
